Decent food, parking available with valet service this place is very crowded almost at all times. Unimaginable crowds at night post 8:30 PM.
Order taking staff doesn’t respond to you unless you call them, but after taking the order, mostly food is served within 5-10 mins which is good. Table clearing and cleaning staff was fast and active. Tea tastes good

There is a huge crowd constantly and the restaurant is busy through out. But they do have a system in place to manage the incoming people, would be great if people too do not behave as if they do not have civic sense and jump queue.

The food was very good, the malai kebabs were awesome, biryani flavour and the aroma was too good. The bun butter though is very ordinary.

We visited this famous biryani restaurant after hearing many recommendations. The biryani was good and tasty, but we didn't find anything particularly special compared to our expectations. Overall, it's a good place to try if you're in the area.

I found this biryani to be highly overrated and unauthentic. The preparation closely resembles tomato rice, complete with visible tomato pieces that do not belong in a traditional biryani. Additionally, the price does not justify the quality of the taste or the small quantity of mutton provided. I echo the sentiments of other customers who have described this dish as tomato rice.

This place is quite popular and often gets a bit crowded. However, the biryani here is truly exceptional and worth the wait. The food overall is delicious, and the service is surprisingly quick despite the busy atmosphere. Considering the quality and quantity, the prices are quite reasonable. And you absolutely must try the mutton somasa and bun butter jam; it's a delightful treat!

Review: Great Restaurant, But Issue with Bakery Service

I would like to share my experience with Buhari Mughal. The restaurant itself is excellent — the infrastructure is truly impressive, the ambiance is well-maintained, and the food quality is very good. Overall, dining here has always been a satisfying experience.

However, we faced a problem specifically with the bakery section. We ordered 4 Black Forest cakes, but after reaching home and opening the box, we found that only 1 cake was inside.

We went back to the bakery and spoke with Haja Kamal, He responded politely and assured us that the matter would be resolved soon. He promised that the issue will be rectified after discussing with the bakery persons and instructed me to send the bill to his WhatsApp regarding the issue. I did the same, but till now He is not yet seen the MSG, Unfortunately, the issue has still not been rectified.

While the restaurant experience remains great, this incident with the bakery service was disappointing. I kindly request customers to double-check their bakery orders before leaving the shop to avoid such situations.

Edited on 25-04-2026 (10:33 am) :- The issue pertained related to Buhari Bakery they refunded 435 Rupees only to my account. Mr. Haja Kamal saved and give life to his words. Thanks to Haja Kamal Sir and Buhari Team.

I had a wonderful dining experience at Buhari Restaurant, Mount Road, Chennai. The food was delicious, fresh, and full of flavour. The staff were friendly, polite, and attentive, providing excellent customer service. The restaurant had a pleasant atmosphere, and everything was well organised.

Overall, I am very happy with the food and hospitality. I highly recommend Buhari Restaurant to anyone looking for a great dining experience in Chennai. Keep up the excellent work!

Had an amazing Chicken Biryani and Mutton Gravy—the taste was superb! 🤤 The Biryani comes with raita, spicy gravy, and a sweet dessert, which makes it a complete and satisfying meal.
The restaurant has a ground-floor section where the prices are quite reasonable, while the first-floor outlet is more expensive. However, the first floor has a much better ambience and is air-conditioned, making it a more comfortable dining experience.

Been to Buhari mutlipe times and have always had either dum tea or zafraani tea. Zafraani tea has a lot of zafraan (saffron) in it which is really good.

The tea itself here is excellent. But when paired with the Persian Maska Bun, it makes for a wonderful combo.

The service is good here. They ensure all food is served timely and are happy to answer questions if any.

Recently visited Buhari and tried their Red Velvet cake, Apple Pie, Chicken Tikka Roll, and Veg Roll. The desserts were the highlight of the visit. The Red Velvet was soft, fresh, and perfectly balanced in sweetness. The Apple Pie was equally impressive, with just the right amount of sweetness and a pleasant texture.
The Veg Roll and Chicken Tikka Roll were good, with a mild and subtle flavor. They weren’t overly spicy, which makes them suitable for those who prefer a lighter taste.
The ambience was pleasant and comfortable. However, the service could definitely be improved as it wasn’t up to the mark during my visit. Overall, a decent experience, especially for dessert lovers.

Not sure what is the hype all about. The only positive this place has the low cost food. But with low cost comes with unhygienic food , poor staff attitude and uncooked raw food.
The way they have placed tandoori chicken on the ground against the badly stained wall says a lot. The tandoori chicken is raw and blood can be seen on some pieces. The mutton biryani unavailability was there so had to go with chicken biryani. Though it was piping hot and straight from fire both rice and chicken was not properly done and tasted raw and hard.

If seems most of influencer are just copying each other content and hardly tasting the food.

Only two wheeler parking available. The are has better biryani spots and much hygienic at around same price.
My experience at Charminar Biryani Centre was absolutely fantastic! ✨ The biryani was incredibly flavorful and cooked to perfection. 🍛 Definitely a top spot for biryani! 👍

Recently I visited to this place with my friend to have a tummy full tasty biriyani.

Customer handling was good by a senior person.

To talk about biriyani taste, It was average on that day with less masala and flavour. Brinjal masala was good. May be my bad luck but last year when I came here The biriyani taste was so good.

I will visit again for sure for more tasty biriyani. Bye.

The staff had a very poor attitude during my visit. Initially, I thought this was just my personal experience, but after reading other reviews, it seems many customers have faced similar issues.
The biryani was good in terms of taste; however, it contained an excessive amount of tomato, which affected the overall balance of flavors.
On a positive note, the restaurant now accepts UPI and Google Pay, so it is no longer cash-only.

Also this isn't broiler chicken so don't be surprised if you find the chicken meat is hard as it's naatu kozhi.

Very below average experience overall. The biryani is not worth the hype — quantity is very low and the place is extremely congested. The only good thing was the country chicken, which had nice flavour. Apart from that, nothing really stood out. Definitely not worth the hype

Cash only! Opens at 3 pm. Mutton brain puff is the best. I forgot to add khova naan because I was so focused on buying baked meat goods. Chicken samosa was okay but mutton samosa had little meat aand more vegetable and oil.

Woww this bakery is a hidden gem!
Loved the samosa's, Hotdog is best and the Honey cake is yummy.
Loved the brownie here. All the food has authentic taste and it's too good.
Youl get best snacks for tea. And other homemade snacks also available here
Like banana chips etc.

I visited here one evening randomly but the Overall my experience here was awesome. I would love to visit again here and enjoy my evening snacks.

Only thing I felt can be better is here they accept only cash.

As we entered the bakery, it was that nostalgic old-school bakery aroma that instantly made me happy. A legendary place that still has all the snacks and sweets many of us grew up eating.
Mutton samosa, bheja puff, kheema naan… we tried a bite of almost everything. Also got home some brun pav. Sometimes it’s these simple old-school places that bring the most joy and comfort. ❤️

Finally made it to albert bakery. It's been on my list for snacks ever since moving to Bangalore. It's such an ancient establishment yet they have not changed anything to keep the heritage. They ONLY ACCEPT CASH! Keep that in mind. We ended up getting the brain puff, mutton samosa, and cheesy chicken puff. Again, over time I feel the food hype of a place does not pay off. The snacks aren't bad but at the same time, they are not out of this world. Don't keep your hope up on the food but do visit for the combination of food and heritage. If you are a sucker for old spots around town, like I am, then you will appreciate this one.

Visited Albert Bakery and loved it. The mutton samosas, khova naan, and lava cakes were all excellent fresh and super tasty. There’s usually a bit of a wait, but it just shows how popular the place is. Only downside: they accept cash only. Definitely worth it for the quality.

If you're in Hyderabad, Alpha Hotel is a great place to experience the city's famous Irani chai and evening snacks. I tried the Osmania and Chand biscuits, and both were fresh and tasty. The Irani chai was good, although it tasted pretty much like the classic Irani chai you'll find at many popular places.

I also tried the Dil Pasand, a sweet pastry filled with pineapple. Personally, I didn't enjoy it because I'm not a fan of pineapple and ordered it by mistake. If you don't like pineapple either, I'd recommend skipping the Dil Pasand.

There isn't a seating area for snacks, so most people enjoy their tea and snacks while standing. However, if you're visiting for biryani, there's a proper seating area inside the restaurant. The place is almost always crowded, especially with people coming just for the famous Irani chai.

I also ordered the egg biryani for takeaway, and it was absolutely delicious—full of flavor, generous in quantity, and completely worth the money.

Overall, Alpha Hotel is definitely worth visiting for its authentic Hyderabad vibe, tasty snacks, Irani chai, and excellent biryani.

This establishment is recognized as one of the city's most historic hotels, situated in a bustling central location. It is highly regarded for its biryani and snack offerings, making it a popular dining destination. The staff provides excellent service, though visitors should anticipate a consistently high volume of patrons. Due to its central urban setting, on-site parking is not provided. Overall, it offers a commendable experience.

Had an average experience at Alpha Hotel & Restaurant. The food was decent and the prices are reasonable, but the overall experience could be better. The place can get quite crowded, especially during peak hours, and the ambience and cleanliness could use some improvement. The location right opposite Secunderabad Railway Station is definitely convenient. Overall, it’s an okay option for a quick meal, especially if you’re around the station, but nothing exceptional.

Famous for its Hyderabadi Biryani, especially mutton biryani.
Popular breakfast items like Keema Roti and Osmania biscuits with Irani chai.
Affordable prices and generous portions.
Convenient location opposite Secunderabad Railway Station.

Visited for lunch to check out the hype. The food quality lives up to its reputation—the  Biryani were top-notch, rich in flavor, and served piping hot. They have separate AC and Non-AC sections, which helps manage the massive crowd better. The only downside is the service speed during rush hour; the staff gets visibly overwhelmed, leading to delays. However, the taste more than makes up for it. Great value for money if you want authentic, old-school Hyderabadi cuisine without burning a hole in your pocket

Visited this place during our Hyderabad trip and tried their biryani. The food was really tasty and full of flavour. The place was very crowded, but the service was good. Overall, a great experience and worth trying if you’re visiting Hyderabad!

We dined in at Bawarchi and ordered the Chicken 65 Biryani. We honestly didn't expect such a disappointing experience from a place known for its biryani.

The biryani was completely flavourless, with almost no masala, making it very bland. The biggest disappointment, however, was the Chicken 65. The pieces were mostly batter and bones, with very little actual chicken. The taste was very poor, and the quality was far below our expectations.

I've also attached photos showing that we couldn't even eat the Chicken 65 pieces because they were so disappointing.

We hope Bawarchi takes this feedback seriously and improves the quality and consistency of its food, especially for dine-in customers.

Veg biryani was nice,with lots of
veggies in the dum. Quantity is more and perfect for 2. Service was too humble. They are known for their hyd style Biryani and price is very cheap I felt but wish their egg biryani was much better with egg in the dum rather than just giving boiled eggs. And it was not really hot(biryani)

This is the ultimate Biryani place. We were a large group and welcomed and seated in reasonable time. The food was all amazing. We had Chicken lollipop and 65, for starters. The loose prawns, Bawarchi special Mutton Curry. Our server was Manoj from Odhissa, and he was very good.
Of course a data is signature Biryani. The food was all good. Even the writer that came with the bean was excellent. The biryani was amazing. Since 1994, the first time I had their biryani, the taste remains the same, may be even better. We will be coming back soon.

Cafe Bahar stands out as one of the best serving biryanis in hyderabad. Had an amazing experience here by having a flavourful and authentic biryani with a mouthful of sweet that tasted yummy. The mutton biryani here is one of the top tier dish everyone should check out.

Ordered mutton biryani and got a plateful of rice and pieces. The taste was very delicious and the flavour was so soothing. The mutton pieces were cooked neat and juicy inside. Then had a sweet which was so juicy and tasty. I visited afternoon so not crowded but in the evenings and nights it will get busier with peak hours.

The service was good and staff were well behaved. The prices were actually affordable and the serving quantity was very much appreciated as I got full by eating a plate.

The best place to checkout for some tasty biryanis and desserts.

This place is decent, I have ordered spl chicken biryani they serve good quantity you can eat 2 people in a single serving.
The taste was awesome and the chicken was so tender.
To be very honest in 400 I have never had this quality and quantity in North India.
Super 👌
The tea was okay okay and Osmania biscuit was delicately good.

One of the iconic Irani restaurants for almost 5 decades, the biryanis and chai are my favourite here. Taste of Chicken Biryani remains consistent since I first visited Cafe Bahar in 1996.

Cafe Bahar runs full almost all the time and you are lucky if you get a table in 15 minutes. Service is pretty fast and billing is even more faster as they need to get the table for the waiting customers.

Leg Piece Chicken Biryani remains my favourite at Cafe Bahar and Kebabs are always top notch. Tandoori Chicken has that spicy taste to suit the typical Hyderabadi Palate, but their Malai Chicken Kebab is excellent.

Overall, it has always been a fantastic visit to Cafe Bahar for last 3 decades

#MysticalFoodie

Last night, I had the pleasure of dining at Cafe Bahar with friends. We started with the Chicken 65 as a starter, which was flavorful, though perhaps not the best choice for those who prefer their food with a serious kick. The star of the show, however, was the Mutton Biryani Jumbo, a dish that comfortably fed our group of six. The biryani was delicious, and the portion size was generous.

The biryani itself was a highlight. The flavors were well-balanced, and the mutton was cooked to perfection. The rice was fluffy and fragrant, making each bite a delight. The Jumbo portion is definitely a good choice if you're dining with a group.

Overall, Cafe Bahar offers a satisfying dining experience. If you're looking for a tasty biryani that's not overly spicy and comes in a generous portion, it's definitely worth a visit. The cost is reasonable for the quality and quantity of food you receive, making it a good value for money.

Prompt service, above average food. The mutton biriyani is good but way too much ghee. Starters are decent. Didn't like Khubani ka Meetha.Parking is a little difficult but the guard assists. Waiting time on weekends can extend upto 30mins.

Chichabas Taj in Fraser Town is a well-known restaurant, especially popular for its mutton and chicken dishes. It is a spacious, big-style restaurant with ample seating that comfortably accommodates families as well as larger groups.

The food tastes good, the staff is friendly and attentive, and the prices are reasonable. Given the quality of the food, the hygiene, and the overall arrangement, the pricing feels justified.

Overall, it’s a reliable and good place to enjoy a hearty non-veg meal. If you’re in the Fraser Town area and looking for a satisfying chicken or mutton dish, Chichabas Taj is definitely worth checking out.

Food is always great at Chichaba's Taj. The Sheekh Kebab, Biryani, and Butter Chicken are highly recommended. Prices are slightly on the higher side, but the taste makes it worth it. I've visited multiple times and never get bored of their food.

In absolute awe with the mutton galouti kebab. Huge fan. Bit disappointed with the mutton keema pav, could have been more flavourful but galouti kebab was so tasty and melt in mouth that it made it worth the visit.

I'd happily come back here again and again just for their Sallu ki Butter Chicken. It's rich, creamy, and perfectly smoky—the balance of flavours is simply outstanding.

As a mutton lover, I was equally impressed with the Mutton Seekh Kebab and Nalli Nihari. Both dishes were incredibly flavorful and cooked to perfection. They pair beautifully with the Kerala Paratha & Khameeri Kulcha, making for a truly satisfying meal.

I've also tried the Mutton Galauti Kebab from their Ramadan special stall, and it was phenomenal—melt-in-the-mouth and packed with flavour.

If you enjoy rich North Indian and Mughlai flavours, this place is definitely worth a visit!

PS - Food always so good that I forget to take pictures, here's one of Sallu ki Butter Chicken 💯

Amazing tasty food. Satisfies your cravings. Mutton adana kebab and mutton koobideh are a must try. Service will be absolutely poor, they literally don't care if you come in or buy from their shop. But if you don't mind all these, for a decent atomosphere, delicious food.

Both the hotel and the banquet hall are nice.
Friendly staff. Food is good enough.
Parking by yourself is a little tight but they have valet parking.

Banquet hall is large enough for 200-250 guests. Has a handy changing room right next to the dias.

Spacious hall . Facilities are ok. But the problem is with the timing they provide hall only for 4 hours and after that each consecutive hour will be charged separately. That is very inconvenient for many people.
The banquet hall is spacious.. Food served was ok.. Good for small and medium gatherings.. the only thing I found was insufficient AC in the rooms.

Very amazing place and my personally favourite one.  We have banquet hall and restaurant here. It is situated in Himayat Nagar opposite the platinum hotel and beside unlimited clothing store.
Second floor is for restaurant and fifth floor is for banquet hall. You get south indian , Chinese , north indian , south indian thali , north indian thali, milkshakes , juices and lot more.  If you are going to go here for the first time you have to try "babai idly" and "steam dosa" and coffee is also Amazing here.
All south indian dishes are amazing and the thalis , north indian too. You get six types of chutneys and sambar too which will be refillied from time to time .
Suggestion : if you are going on Saturdays and Sundays please pre book the table so that you don't have to wait.

Good Tasty Tiffin items with their famous speciality the 'chutneys'... mouth watering total 6 to 9 types of chutneys were presented along with every item ordered. Ambience is awsome with good timely service. Usually on holidays the rush is more and you have to wait really long. Very less seating space is available for waiting persons...the owner must take care of this issue. Except this The 'CHTNEYS' IS MUST VISIT place for all foodies.....

Went there on a weekday evening and hence found a table to enjoy their classic DBC icecream with a friend. The quantity of their DBC icecream is really generous and can be easily enjoyed by 2-3 folks. Its a Sundar which comes with a generous amount of icecream scoops, soft spongy brownies, cherries and their classic chocolate fudge and topped with crushed salted nuts at the end. Very very yummy, crunchy, soft with heavenly mix of textures. Must try for chocolate lovers !!

Tried the ice creams here and absolutely loved the taste and quality! The flavors were rich, creamy, and perfectly balanced — especially with the chocolate topping and crunchy nuts. The presentation was also really good and the place had a nice vibe. Great spot to satisfy your dessert cravings. Would definitely visit again!

Honestly, I felt this place was quite overrated. The ice cream taste is good, but it’s no different from what you would get at any other decent outlet. The major issue is the pricing—it is quite expensive compared to others, especially for a self-service parlour. For these prices, you expect a premium experience, but they serve everything in basic disposable paper cups rather than actual glassware, with hardly any sincere presentation. To make matters worse, the seating comfort is lacking. Fans are not available in every corner, and the tables we managed to secure were completely outside the fan zone, making it uncomfortably warm.

I recently visited this ice cream shop and tried the Fruit Jackpot priced at ₹210, and overall it was a satisfying experience. The dessert was definitely worth the money. The portion size was generous, and the combination of fresh fruits with ice cream was refreshing and enjoyable. The flavors were well balanced, and the quality of the ice cream was good.
One thing I really liked about this place is the wide range of ice cream options available. There are plenty of flavors and combinations to choose from, which makes it an exciting place for anyone who loves trying different desserts. The menu offers a good variety, so customers can explore multiple options depending on their preference.
However, one area where the store can improve is the air conditioning inside the outlet. During my visit, it felt quite warm inside, which slightly affected the overall comfort while enjoying the dessert. Maintaining proper air conditioning would make the experience much more pleasant for customers, especially considering that people usually spend some time inside while eating ice cream.
Overall, it’s a good place to enjoy desserts with friends or family. With a small improvement in the store ambience, the experience could become even better. Definitely worth visiting if you enjoy ice cream.

Death by Chocolate is a must-try if you’re in Bangalore. Priced at ₹250, it’s easily enough for two—and you might still not finish it. The portion is massive. Quick service and a chill, laid-back vibe make it a great spot to hang out with frnds.

The place is well designed and welcoming. While I’ve always been a big fan of Hyderabadi Biryani, the Dindigul Thalappakatti Biryani was absolutely exquisite. It was meticulously prepared, beautifully presented, and remarkably flavorful, with top-notch ingredients and a perfect balance of textures and spices.
However, the portion sizes felt small for the price — a standard serving contained only two small pieces of meat.
The Mango Pudding for dessert tasted exactly like khojri (the first three days of milk from a cow after giving birth), with added mango flavour.
On the downside, the staff were inattentive, orders were delayed, and there was no proper response when we raised our concerns. Parking was also a hassle.

Very poor quality.
We had order mutton chops and mutton biryani (2servings).

To start with the chops was only 2pcs while the biryani was horrible. It has 4 pieces but all bones only, no meat. There was chunks of crushed bone mixed in rice.(Rs.575)

Very less quantity of food served for the price charged!

Visited this branch after a year, and the biryani and tawa fish still taste just as good as before. The flavor remains consistent and satisfying. However, the prices have increased and feel a bit high for the quantity served. For the taste, though, it’s something we may have to compromise on. The service is good, but since most of the staff are North Indian, we had to repeat our requests a couple of times. The ambiance is pleasant overall. Recommended
Now a days the taste was so bad I tried 555 Briyani worst experiences ever

Good food great staff
Nool parata is amazing

A decent biryani and flavourful tandoori chicken. The Mango Punch Cooler was incredibly refreshing, though a bit overpriced.

If you're looking for a late-night food spot in Bengaluru, Empire is always a reliable option. With an outlet in almost every corner of the city and a legacy of over 60 years, it's no surprise the restaurants stay packed.

That said, the service could be better. A few staff members came across as arrogant and careless while taking orders, which affected the overall experience. Still, for a satisfying late-night meal, Empire remains a go-to choice.

The staff were friendly, polite, and provided good hospitality throughout the visit. While the chicken biryani was decent, it didn't quite stand out. Felt like it was normal rice. However, the chicken kebab, alfaham, butter naan, and chicken korma were much better and were the highlights of the meal. The atmosphere of the hotel was average and fairly comfortable, though nothing particularly remarkable. The only downside was that the prices felt a bit high compared to the overall experience. Overall, it was a pleasant visit with good food and service, especially if you're looking to try their grilled and curry dishes. Overall, it was an okay stay, but better value for money would make it more appealing.

I was trying to order online and wanted clarity on dinner dishes, this guy Ashfaque picks the call and has no information or idea about the food, why is he picking up the calls in the first place. He promised to get someone to call me back but no-one did so I ended up ordering from different restaurant... Disappointed I remember the service used to be more professional earlier....

The food was absolutely delicious and full of flavour. 🍽️ The service was excellent, especially thanks to Jafar, who was very friendly, attentive, and helpful throughout the visit. The atmosphere was also pleasant and comfortable. Overall, a great dining experience—definitely worth visiting! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Taste is good but one staff seems like manager looks so arrogant to our group.
First I wanna return the menu back and that guy walked to that way and stopped walking then he told the waiter to get it back by pointing his finger to me and he didn’t say anything to me.
Just feel like Oh wow how rude you are!
If you can’t take it then you should tell me “please wait a moment the waiter will come to get it” or something else, shouldn’t walk pass like this and I saw he isn’t busy at that time.
Maybe he is Egotistical person and thought like he is manager can’t touch the menu.
In other restaurants manager will take menu back and send to waiter or another staff because customer already gave it in front of him.

Waiting for food for a very long time, another group came after us but they got food before us.

And we found hair in coin parotta so we called the waiter to change it but that manager suddenly came and tried to stop the waiter and asked. He didn’t asked customer first for what happened. We really felt racism from him because we’re from Southeast Asia maybe he thought we’re from Tibet who live here that’s why he discriminated with us.
But they changed the new plate for us

One thing that I like is the real time screen on TV to show about inside the kitchen. That’s so good to make sure your food is clean. I really appreciated and so impressed about it and would like to take a picture for the review but they told me to delete it.

I’m not sure he’s a manager or not but he acted like that. The thin guy with suit jacket.
But I would like to tell you… Even Bastian restaurant we already spent a lot of money there so “don’t look down to the customer!”

Fanoos still rolls like a legend 🌯🔥

Visited after more than a decade, and it felt like meeting an old friend who somehow hasn’t aged. The place is much bigger now and they even have seating, but the magic remains exactly the same. Their rolls are still outrageously delicious, especially the chicken liver rolls, which continue to be our absolute favorite. Juicy, spicy, perfectly wrapped little cylinders of happiness.
Parking can be a bit of a puzzle, but the security guard somehow manages to find a spot for everyone with ninja-level efficiency.
Rare to see a place grow bigger without losing its soul. Fanoos has done exactly that.

Tried the beef seekh kebab and the fanoos chicken roll. Both lacked flavour, which was very disappointing. The roti in the roll was tough as well. Must say that price was very affordable.

Another issue was the hygiene. The place seems quite dirty and food containers were sitting open as well.

Not sure if the place is taken over by new staff, but it's gone down. They don't care about the customer. I ordered chicken kebab takeaway and after 30 minutes when I went and asked if it was ready. I was asked what did u order. And to beat it all I got 3 small pieces of chicken and a few scrapes costed me 160 rs. Very disappointed not worth going there anymore. Had lunch at Junior Kuppanna, Anna Nagar, after seeing their outside banner mentioning Chicken Meals at ₹320. Based on that displayed price, I ordered the chicken meals. However, when the bill came, I was charged ₹420.

When I questioned the cashier about the difference, he simply said that the banner had been displayed by mistake, that they would change it, and that I should pay ₹420. I explained that if the actual price was ₹420, I could have chosen another dish or even another restaurant. But he repeatedly insisted that I pay the higher amount. When I said that I would mention this experience in a Google review, his response was simply, “No worries, do that.”

The issue is not just the ₹100 difference. If a restaurant displays a price outside the premises, customers naturally expect that price to be honoured. A pricing mistake should be handled professionally, especially when the customer has ordered based on the displayed price.

MTR (Mavalli Tiffin Room) – A True Taste of Bangalore’s Culinary Heritage
​If you want to experience the authentic food culture and heritage of Bangalore, a visit to MTR is absolute must. It is less of a standard meal and more of a cultural rite of passage for food lovers.

​Rava Idli (Must-Try): Hands down the star of the show. Pouring the warm, rich ghee over the soft rava idli wakes up your taste buds instantly. It is worth the visit alone.
​Masala Dosa, Khara Bath & Podi Masala Dosa: Decent overall, but keep your expectations grounded. While good, they don't quite hit the legendary mark that the rava idli sets.

​Beat the Crowds: Avoid weekends if possible, as it gets extremely packed.
​Seating System: Head straight upstairs to put your name down on the waiting list as soon as you arrive.
​MTR offers a timeless look into Old Bangalore's rich breakfast traditions. Definitely worth a visit for the experience!

I also ordered Double Ka Meetha for dessert, and that was absolutely delicious — a must-try! The restaurant also served sirca onion along with the meal, which was a good touch.

The ambience was pleasant and comfortable. Overall, I had a good time and would recommend this place, especially if you enjoy authentic Hyderabadi biryani flavors.

Savoury and mouth-watering dishes with excellent flavors that are sure to satisfy your taste buds. The ambience is pleasant and inviting, making it a great place to dine. One of the best parts is that you can customize the spice level according to your preference. The staff is professional and courteous, although the service can be a little slow during busy hours. Overall, it's a great restaurant and definitely worth a visit.

Paradise Biryani is a solid choice for authentic Hyderabadi biryani. The flavors are good, portions are filling, and the overall experience is satisfying. It can get very crowded, so expect some waiting time, but the food makes up for it. Would visit again.
But service is really quick inspite of so much crowd and that’s amazing.
Biryani tasted very good with authentic flavors and the service was prompt. The dining atmosphere was truly exceptional.

For vegetarian people, honestly it’s not that great. As soon as we enter, there’s a strong non-veg smell everywhere. For non-vegetarian people it may be super, but for vegetarians one-time experience is enough. Prices are also too high — even a 1 litre water bottle costs ₹60 there, while outside it’s ₹20. Veg biryani in Hyderabad usually costs around ₹100–250, but there it’s ₹319.

It’s a very famous biryani place, no doubt, but mainly suitable for non-veg lovers only.

Visited Pista House Shahalibanda on a Sunday around 4 PM. It was quite busy, so we had to wait for a while, but the food was definitely worth it. The items we ordered were delicious and served fresh. The staff were polite, well-behaved, and handled the rush efficiently. Overall, a great dining experience.

I had the pleasure of dining at Pista house which is an iconic place for authentic hyderabadi cuisine near Charminar.
I had Zafrani Paneer biryani, Paneer majestic, Shahtoot malai and Khubani ka meetha. The biryani and majestic were exceptional with mild distinct flavours of spices and saffron.  Shahtoot malai was also rich in taste but the Khubani ka meetha was bit of a let down.
The service was outstanding and prompt.
Overall a great experience!

I would suggest planning your visit before 11 PM ⏰ because we went a bit late and the biryani was limited. I tried the Mutton Biryani 🍛 and Mutton Chops 🥩 – both were really good! The chicken dishes I tried were just average.

Visited Rahhams once again—a place well known for its excellent biryani. This is our go-to spot whenever we crave a truly good biryani, and we’ve been coming here for years.
Rahhams is known for serving authentic local Bangalore-style biryani made with zeera rice (not basmati), which I absolutely love. The flavor is very local and distinctly different from other styles like Hyderabadi, Lucknowi, Dakhni, Donne, etc.
I’ve known this place for over 20+ years, right from when it originally opened as Richies and was later renamed to Rahhams. On this visit, we tried their signature Mutton Biryani, Pahadi Chicken, and Mutton Chops.
As always, the biryani was super delicious. The Pahadi Chicken was extremely tender, coated with the right balance of masala, slightly tangy, and left a lingering flavor that really teases the taste buds.
Highly recommended if you’re looking for a true local Bangalore-style “shaadi-ki” biryani. Looking forward to visiting again!

Rahhams Families International is making a meaningful impact through its activities and support for families. The team is friendly, organized, and committed to helping people. Wishing them continued success!

Though taste & flavour was gud, I would go back to Bai Biryani ✌️

I recently visited Savoury Seashell Restaurant, and it turned out to be a truly satisfying dining experience.
We started with Crispy Cauliflower and Samak Meshwi (catfish). Both were delicious, but the Samak Meshwi was the absolute standout. The fish was perfectly grilled, juicy, and packed with flavour — easily one of the best grilled fish dishes I’ve had. The crispy cauliflower was equally impressive, crunchy on the outside and well-seasoned.
For the mains, I paired Kerala Paratha with Murg Musallam (half), and it was a complete taste bomb. The paratha was soft and flaky, complementing the rich, flavourful gravy of the murg musallam beautifully. Every bite was indulgent and satisfying.

Overall, the food quality was excellent, especially the grilled fish and murg musallam. Definitely a place worth visiting if you enjoy flavourful seafood.

Hotel Shadab is one of the oldest and Legendary outlet for authentic Hyderabadi cuisines and dishes. Located near to Charminar it attracts a major number of food lovers who try all kinds of foods here. It's basically have the old city vibe and the special foods that makes it worth the visit.

Their mutton biryani is hailed as the best ever in hyderabad. The paaya is so delicious and nutritious aa well which they serve in the mornings. It's usually always covered but still it's worth the wait to hace the taste of it.

During the Ramzan season it's get totally crowded like very much. They serve the delicious Mutton Haleem which so aromatic and delicious. They offer many other foods which are very popular and you can try them all.

A totally worth the visit to have some flavourful foods of old hyderabad. The prices are decent and the portions are good at the price. Top quality serving and serices provided.

Unmissable Feast!

​You can't visit Hyderabad without eating at Hotel Shadab, and it completely lived up to the hype! We visited on a Monday around 4 PM, and the place was still fully packed—a true testament to how popular and iconic it is.

​Biryani: The absolute star of the show. Extremely flavorful, perfectly spiced, and rich in authentic Hyderabadi flavor.
​Qubani Ka Meetha: A massive hit! Sweet, rich, and the ultimate way to wrap up the meal.

​Despite the heavy crowd and bustling vibe, the experience was well worth it. If you want an authentic taste of Hyderabad, Shadab is an absolute must-visit!

Had Mutton Biryani at Hotel Shadab and it was absolutely delicious. The biryani had great flavor, tender mutton pieces, and authentic Hyderabad taste. Definitely one of the places to try when visiting Hyderabad.
One thing to note is that the quantity is quite generous. If you are visiting as a group of two, I would recommend ordering one biryani first and then deciding if you need another. It may be enough for many people, and this helps avoid food wastage.
The service was good, and the restaurant has a lively atmosphere. Overall, a satisfying dining experience and a place I would happily visit again.

Tried both the Chicken and Mutton Biryani, and they were full of flavor with a wonderful aroma. The special boneless Chicken Biryani was especially outstanding and definitely worth trying.

The only downside is the waiting time. You may need to wait around 20 minutes to get a table and another 20 minutes for your food to be served. It’s best to avoid peak lunch and dinner hours if you’re in a hurry.

The quantity is quite generous,two biryanis are enough for three people, so plan your order accordingly. Overall, the food quality, taste, and portion size were excellent.

Hyderabad and biryani are truly a match made in heaven, and Hotel Shadab proved it to us. Located near Charminar, the place is always crowded, so we reached by Uber and that made things easy. We were a group of six and got a big table without much wait, which was perfect because we were starving after our Charminar visit.

We ordered mutton biryani, Changezi kebab, mutton barra, and meat paratha. Honestly, the biryani was the star of the meal. I have tried biryani from several so-called famous places, but this one easily beats them all. The rice was fragrant, the meat was tender, and every bite felt rich and satisfying. The kebabs were juicy, smoky, and full of flavour, with great quality in every dish.

We also tried goli soda, which was both a fun visual treat and refreshing to drink. My second favourite was the meat paratha. I had asked about it at many places before, and most said no, but here they served it, and it was absolutely wow.

If you are in Hyderabad and want unforgettable biryani, Hotel Shadab is a must-visit. The service was quick, the portions generous, and the overall experience felt completely worth it.☺️

Nevertheless it was well marinated and cooked. Long grained, fluffy, flavoured rice and their baigan bartha were the highlights. Bartha was tangy and nutty because of peanuts.
Staff could be a little more responsive. The ambience needs a lot more than fix.
Overall, food here will not disappoint you, if lacks in service and ambience are ignored.

The mosque derives its evocative name from the tradition of illuminating its vast prayer hall with a thousand oil lamps, creating a mesmerizing spectacle that has become part of local legend.

Architecturally, the mosque is a striking example of Indo-Islamic design, featuring multiple domes and tall minarets that rise prominently above the bustling Anna Salai area.

The main prayer hall is spacious and adorned with Quranic inscriptions, while separate areas are designated for men and women. The mosque complex also includes a Dargah dedicated to Imam Hussain (Raziyallahu Anhu), the revered grandson of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, further enhancing its spiritual significance for the Shia community.

The Thousand Lights Mosque is not only a vibrant center for daily worship but also a focal point during Muharram, when thousands gather to commemorate the martyrdom of Imam Hussain. The atmosphere during these observances is solemn, with the mosque beautifully lit and filled with the sounds of prayer and reflection.

Visitors are welcomed, provided they dress modestly and observe the decorum expected in a place of worship. The mosque’s central location makes it easily accessible, and it remains open from early morning until late evening, inviting both devotees and those interested in its history and architecture to experience its unique ambiance.

Beyond its religious functions, the mosque is a symbol of Chennai’s pluralistic heritage and serves as a reminder of the city’s deep-rooted connections to diverse faiths and traditions. Its enduring presence, historical roots, and architectural grandeur make it a must-visit for anyone seeking to understand the cultural and spiritual fabric of Chennai.

We recently visited The Minar, Jewel of Nizam at Golconda Hotels with our family, and it turned out to be a wonderful dining experience.

One thing that could definitely be improved is the reservation process. I had made an online reservation but never received a confirmation call. When we arrived on the weekend, we were disappointed to learn that no tables were available despite the booking. We had to make another reservation and return on next day. It was an inconvenience, and I hope the management streamlines the reservation system to avoid such situations for future guests.

That said, our second visit was absolutely worth it. The restaurant has a beautiful royal ambiance that reflects the rich heritage of Hyderabad. The atmosphere is elegant, comfortable and perfect for family dinners or special occasions.

We started with a vegetarian starter, followed by the signature Patthar Ka Gosht, which was simply outstanding. The meat was incredibly tender, flavorful and cooked to perfection. For the main course, we ordered Paneer Makhan Masala along with a selection of freshly baked breads, and every dish was delicious. The Virgin Piña Colada was refreshing and one of the best mocktails we had during our visit.

The prices are slightly on the higher side, but the quality of the food, presentation, ambiance, and overall dining experience make it worthwhile.

Overall, we had a memorable dining with our family. If the restaurant improves its reservation management, the experience would be nearly perfect. Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Hyderabadi cuisine in a luxurious setting.

I recently visited Jewel of Nizam with high expectations, especially given its reputation and beautiful setting. While the ambience truly lives up to the hype, the overall dining experience was disappointing.

The property is stunning, with elegant interiors and a royal atmosphere that makes it a great place for a special evening. Unfortunately, the service did not match the standard you’d expect from a premium restaurant.

The waitstaff were rarely visible on the dining floor and were mostly inside, which meant we had to repeatedly look for someone whenever we needed anything. Even something as basic as getting drinking water required multiple follow-ups. Throughout the meal, we found ourselves waiting for assistance rather than enjoying the experience.

The food itself was average. It wasn’t bad, but it certainly didn’t justify the price point or the restaurant’s reputation. A place with such a premium ambience should ideally deliver equally impressive food and attentive service.

Overall, Jewel of Nizam excels in ambience but falls short on hospitality and service. I hope the management focuses on improving staff attentiveness and guest experience, because with such a beautiful venue, better service could make a significant difference.

The mutton biryani here is pure love and an absolute must-try! The flavors are spot on, and serving it on a fresh banana leaf adds that authentic traditional touch that elevates the entire dining experience. We also tried the mutton balls—personally, I found them fairly average, though my friend really enjoyed them. Still, the biryani alone makes this place well worth a visit!

Nagarjuna is one of those famous Andhra-style restaurants in Bangalore that we’ve always heard about, so we finally visited the Indiranagar outlet last week for lunch.

We went on a Saturday afternoon and the place was packed! The restaurant has multiple floors and even the area around the parking was quite crowded. We waited for around 10 minutes before getting a table.

We ordered two full meals, which were served on a banana leaf. Once we were seated, everything started coming in hot and fresh — rice, sambar, rasam, poriyal, buttermilk, payasam, papad and the other accompaniments. The papad was unlimited as well.

We started with the podi and avakkai, and honestly, that combination was amazing! 🔥 But the biggest highlight of the entire meal for me was the koottu. It was SO good that I had it twice and kept asking for more. 😍 The sambar was also really tasty, the rasam was decent, and the buttermilk was refreshing. They also served a nice thick curd separately along with payasam.

Overall, it was a proper satisfying, heavy South Indian meal. I ate so much that I went home and literally had a good nap afterwards! 😂❤️

Coming to the price, it is definitely on the expensive side — one full meal costs around ₹350+. But if you go really hungry and want to have a proper unlimited-style Andhra meal, you can definitely make the most of it.

Overall, a very filling and satisfying lunch experience. If you’re someone who enjoys Andhra-style meals, Nagarjuna is definitely a place worth trying at least once.

Food is amazing but very spicy. I ordered chicken roast that turned out to be very spicy and salty. Staff politely replaced it with chicken kebab. Loved the meals and biryani. I would like to visit again.

Had a nice experience at Nagarjuna Restaurant, Indiranagar. The food was delicious, the ambience was good, and the service was quick.

One of Bengaluru's most popular destinations for authentic Andhra cuisine, Nagarjuna has been serving its signature dishes since 1984. I had been wanting to try their popular Veg Meals, so we visited on a Sunday afternoon. As expected, the restaurant was packed. Fortunately, I had booked in advance, so getting a table wasn't an issue.

The meals were served on a traditional banana leaf and included Dal (Pappu), Sambar, Rasam, one vegetable, chutney, papad, a sweet (Payasam), curd, and buttermilk.

To begin with, the Dal (Pappu) with rice was good. However, the Aloo Sabji was average and didn't pair particularly well with the rice. To complement the meal, we ordered one of their dry mutton dishes. The mutton pieces were good enough and flavorful, though not exceptionally tender. The preparation was slightly dry, and a little more juiciness would have made the dish even better.

The curd and buttermilk were fresh, while the Sambar and Rasam complemented the rice well. The Payasam was decent and rounded off the meal nicely.

One thing to note is that extra curd is charged separately, and the staff informs you about this while taking your order. I'm not sure if the same applies to the sweet.

Even though the restaurant was completely packed, there was no compromise on the service. The staff managed the crowd efficiently, and the overall dining experience was smooth.

Overall, while the experience was good, I somehow didn't leave feeling completely satisfied with the meal. A few dishes could have been better, and I felt there was room for improvement. I'll give Nagarjuna another try on my next visit and hope to have a better experience.

Beautiful and historic mosque in Triplicane. It is a large mosque and is very well and strictly maintained by the authorities. The cleanliness and overall upkeep are impressive, making it a peaceful place for offering prayers.

The mosque was built in 1795 and is considered the largest mosque in Triplicane. Despite its age, the place has been maintained very well while preserving its historical character.

The mosque was recently renovated in March this year in 2026, which has further improved its appearance and facilities. The prayer hall is fully air-conditioned with over 60 ton capacity, making it much more comfortable for worshippers, especially during Chennai's hot weather.

It can accommodate 5000 persons at a time for prayer. They open tents in ground area for Jummah prayer and Eid's to get covered from Sun. They also have dedicated phone application to download in mobile phone for information.

One thing I particularly appreciate is that many of the administrative staff and people involved in operating and maintaining the mosque are Hindu/non-Muslim, yet they are managing their responsibilities very well and maintaining the place in a respectful and proper manner. It is genuinely good to see people from different religious backgrounds working together and contributing to the peaceful functioning and maintenance of such an important religious place.

This kind of cooperation shows religious harmony and mutual respect, especially in an area with several important religious and historical landmarks.

I visited Walajah Big Mosque during Maghrib prayer. The mosque is located in a predominantly Muslim area of Triplicane, Chennai, not very far from Marina Beach. The environment around the mosque feels lively yet spiritually calm.

The wudu (ozu) and toilet facilities are clean and well-maintained, which makes it comfortable for visitors. At present, there is no separate female prayer room, but the gatekeeper informed me that it is under renovation and should be available within about one month.

There is also a nearby dargah sharif, which visitors can easily visit along with the mosque. I reached the mosque by auto-rickshaw, which can go directly into the courtyard, making access easy even for first-time visitors.

Walajah Big Mosque is one of the oldest and most significant mosques in Chennai, built in the 18th century during the rule of Nawab Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah, the Nawab of Arcot. The mosque is named after him and stands as a symbol of the rich Islamic heritage of Triplicane. Over the years, it has remained a central place for worship, learning, and community gatherings, preserving its traditional character while adapting to modern needs.

The area around the mosque is also famous for its halal food streets, with many eateries offering traditional Muslim cuisine, making it a great place to explore after prayers.
